text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam's fisheries hauled in 454,000 tonnes of seafood in the first four months of this year. The industry also exported $235 million worth of products, an increase of 18 percent over the same period of last year.
-- Vietnam and Japan will step up cooperation, especially in trade and investment, Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said on his return from an official visit to Japan.

-- Ten out of 20 foreign investment projects worth some $474 million of Saigon Trading Corporation (Satra) have been disbanded due to ineffective operation, lack of financial ability or capital contribution violations, according to a report by Satra.
-- The 8th Vietnamese Women's Congress, which opened on Monday, will focus on how to adjust and supplement regulations of the functioning, objectives and structure of the Vietnam Women's Union.
-- Pham The Duyet, head of the Party Mass Mobilization Commission, visited monks and Buddhist clergymen in a Hanoi pagoda to mark Buddha's birthday celebrations.
-- A military shell warehouse exploded on the outskirts of Ho Chi Minh City on Sunday. Two people died, 45 were wounded and nearly 1,000 houses were damaged.
